title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government outlines its plan to align artificial intelligence with public standards, building on the 2020 committee report. It commits to greater transparency, accountability, and regulatory measures to protect citizens’ interests.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will oversee and set rules for using AI in exams and qualifications. It aims to keep tests fair, reliable and free from bias, while also protecting students and educators from potential misuse of AI.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report explores how copyright‑protected works are used in training and building AI systems and assesses the legal and economic effects of those practices. It offers recommendations to balance creators’ rights with innovation and suggests policy changes that promote fair and responsible use of copyrighted materials in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has released a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” In it, the government outlines its commitment to addressing the report’s concerns and highlights planned measures to enhance AI safety, foster innovation, and strengthen regulatory oversight.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the scope, objectives, and responsibilities of a committee charged with examining how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards, including the key questions it will investigate. It also provides FAQs to clarify expectations for AI tools in terms of governance, compliance, and ethical considerations.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of Artificial Intelligence, outlining its perspective on current AI policy challenges. The submission highlights the organization’s concerns and offers recommendations for how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence changes the rules governing medical products, ensuring they remain safe and effective. It applies the AI White Paper's principles to guide transparency, accountability, and risk assessment in medical AI development and deployment.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential leader in AI for a country of our size. It outlines plans and priorities to develop, deploy, and manage AI technologies that enhance national security and operational capabilities.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will work with the transport sector to harness the benefits of AI technologies. It also details how to manage and mitigate the risks that come with deploying AI in transport.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report outlines how copyrighted material is being used to train AI models and the legal framework governing it. It highlights compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, including findings on licensing, fair use, and ongoing challenges.
